open_obligations: Check that Kenton et al.'s QuALITY subset is comparable in difficulty to Khan et al.'s HARD subset.
Note different debater models (Gemini Pro 1.5 versus GPT-4-Turbo) and judges.
Check whether Kenton et al. use a quote verification tool.
out.other_title: Human judges 88% with debate vs 78% consultancy; LLM judges 76% vs 54% (naive 60% / 48%)
out.rationale: Khan et al. report that, for the most persuasive models, non-expert LLM judges reach 76% with debate versus 54% with consultancy on QuALITY HARD. Kenton et al. report that on extractive tasks (QuALITY, BoolQ, GPQA-extractive) where only debaters see the article, judges are more accurate under debate than under consultancy and QA without article, except that the weakest judge Gemma7B does no better with debate than with QA without article; both use LLM debaters with privileged article access.
out.scope: proposed SUPPORTS: whether debate beats consultancy for non-expert LLM judges on information-asymmetric reading comprehension

text: The paper reports that on extractive tasks, QA with article is best for all judge models, and judges are more accurate under debate than under consultancy and QA without article, except for the weakest judge Gemma7B, which does no better with debate than with QA without article.
title: Extractive tasks: debate gives higher judge accuracy than consultancy and QA without article, except for the weakest judge Gemma7B
